title: Racial final pass (Oct 26): Human Spirit 10%, Dwarf +1% hit, Orc pets +5%, Tauren Endurance 5% HP
claim: Oct 26 dev notes: Human Ruthless 2% -> 1% crit and The Human Spirit 5% -> 10% Spirit; Dwarf Earth Fury removed, new Artisan's Precision +1% spell and melee hit; Orc Savage (1% crit) removed and Command back (+5% Hunter/Warlock pet damage); Tauren Endurance now only +5% Health; Skyborne Wind-Blessed haste 3% -> 2%.
detail: Kaivax post #7 in the beta development notes thread, posted Oct 26 ~20:35 UTC, the night before name reservation. Racials only; no class, quest or XP changes. Night Elf, Gnome, Undead and Troll are not mentioned, so their Oct 15 versions stand (n:20261017-racials-oct15; Blood Fury 3 min and Troll regen 20% unchanged). Weapon-specialization racials stay removed. Leveling impact: Human Spirit regen +10% (less drinking/eating for Human Priests/Mages/Warlocks), Orc Hunter/Warlock pet +5% damage, Dwarf/Human Hunters lose crit but Dwarf gains +1% hit. Applies at launch (Nov 4); there was no client build, so this is server-side.

title: Tauren Plainsrunning: 2% per stack, up to 60% run speed on foot; no mounted bonus
claim: Tauren Plainsrunning now gives 2% movement speed per stack (was 1%) up to 60% (was 30%) and no longer adds 3% mounted speed; with the previous build-up rate (1 stack per 5 s of uninterrupted running, 30 stacks) the full 60% takes about 150 s of running.
detail: Official numbers: Oct 26 dev notes. Stack mechanics are from Warcraft Tavern's Tauren guide (pre-Oct 26 version): one stack per 5 s of running, standing still 1 s drops one stack, taking a hit drops 6 stacks, does not stack with Ghost Wolf or Aspect of the Cheetah, works indoors. Forum players also quote ~150 s to max. Blizzard did not say the rate changed, so assume 30 stacks x 5 s. 60% equals the level-40 ground mount, so a Tauren covering long runs (Barrens, Thousand Needles, Desolace, corpse runs) before a mount travels almost at mount speed after 2.5 min. Running in combat or with frequent stops keeps it low. Check the build-up rate on day 1. The Oct 15 version (+3% mounted speed, stutter-stepping no longer keeps it) is replaced.

title: Skyborne: Skysight 15% speed (30% for 1 h when Charged at a convergence); Read Leyline 50% regen (100% when Attuned)
claim: Skysight now gives 15% movement speed for 15 s (was 10%); using it at an elemental convergence grants Charged for 1 hour, during which Skysight gives 30%. Read Leyline gives 50% health/mana regen for 15 s (was 100%), can't be used under Innervate, and at a Ley Line grants Attuned for 1 hour (100% regen). Charged and Attuned persist through death.
detail: Oct 26 dev notes. Leveling impact: a Windshaper (Horde) Skyborne who passes an elemental convergence gets a 1-hour 30% sprint on the racial's cooldown; a High Order (Alliance) Skyborne gets full-strength drinking/eating regen for an hour after touching a Ley Line. The Oct 15 build added convergence and Ley Line spawns in most zones. Cooldowns are not given in the notes.

title: Downtime racials: Troll Rapid Regeneration 50% HP / 6 s / 3 min; Cannibalize 35% HP and mana / 10 s / 2 min
claim: Players quoting the launch tooltips: Troll Rapid Regeneration restores 50% of max health over 6 s on a 3-minute cooldown (out of combat), and Undead Cannibalize restores 7% health and mana every 2 s for 10 s (35% each) on a 2-minute cooldown, humanoid or undead corpses only.
detail: Forum thread 'Troll feels mandatory for a lot of classes' (Oct 27). Per minute: Cannibalize ~17.5% HP and mana, Rapid Regen ~16.7% HP. Both cut eating/drinking between pulls; Cannibalize also restores mana. Numbers are tooltip readings by players, not measured; no staff reply.

title: Forever GuideMate: free GPL questing guide addon with Alliance/Horde 1-60 routes and class-quest guides
claim: Forever GuideMate (CurseForge, v0.7.2, Oct 22, ~2.8k downloads, GPLv3, source github.com/TylerAkins/forever-guide-mate) has Alliance and Horde 1-60 'casual' routes, class quests for all nine classes, dungeon quest chains and a library books guide.
detail: Alpha. Routes aim at casual efficiency, not speed. Uses Blizzard map pins or TomTom. Its open data could be read for quest order and class-quest steps; no adapter yet.

title: QuestPact: addon that shares quest progress and lets you follow a partner's turn-in route
claim: QuestPact (github.com/Rainsphere/QuestPact, interface 16001) shows quests shared with your group and partners, lets the leader skip quests for everyone, and has a catch-up window listing a partner's turn-ins in order and zone so you can follow their route.
detail: New Oct 27. Useful for duo leveling: see which quests a partner lacks before turn-ins. Uses Questie names if installed. Untested on live.
